title: Some towns still stand, some were mown down.
subtitle: Looking back at the ruins as a lesson
then: After the stories of the prophets and their nations, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ these are {idea}news of the towns We relate to you{/idea}. Of them, some still stand, and {trap}some have been reaped, totally destroyed{/trap}, like a harvested field.
now: You watch a documentary about an ancient city in ruins, then switch to the next show. Or you walk past a closed-down factory that once employed half the town. {idea}Pause on it.{/idea} Every ruin is a question about how its people lived.
old: Stories of destroyed nations are just history.
new: These stories are told so I look at my own life while there is still time.
try: Next time you see ruins or an abandoned building, ask yourself one honest question about your own habits.

title: We did not wrong them; they wronged themselves.
subtitle: False gods added nothing but loss
then: Allah says {idea}We did not wrong them{/idea} when We destroyed them; {trap}they wronged themselves{/trap} by rejecting their messengers. When the command came, their idols could not help or save them. Mujahid and Qatadah said those gods only added loss.
now: You stayed up gaming instead of studying, then blamed the exam. You spent on credit, then blamed the bank. {idea}Some wounds are self-inflicted.{/idea} Seeing that is not shame; it is the start of change.
old: When things go badly, it is usually someone else's fault.
new: Allah wrongs no one; much of my harm comes from my own choices, which I can change.
try: Name one problem you keep blaming on others and write one thing you did that fed it.

title: Respite is long, but the seizing is sure.
subtitle: Delay is not escape
then: This is how Allah seizes towns that do wrong, and {trap}His seizing is painful and severe{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, he cannot escape, and then he recited this verse. {idea}What He did to them, He does to any like them.{/idea}
now: You have been cutting corners for months and nothing has happened. No audit, no consequence. It starts to feel safe. {idea}Respite is not approval.{/idea} It is time given to turn back while turning back is still possible.
old: If nothing bad has happened yet, what I am doing must be fine.
new: Delay is a mercy and a warning, not a sign that I got away with it.
try: Stop one small wrong today that you have been getting away with.

title: A Day everyone is gathered and everyone sees.
subtitle: The ruins point to a bigger gathering

row.title: a sign
sub: for those who fear the next life

row.title: those who fear
sub: the punishment of the next life

then: The destruction of deniers and rescue of believers is {idea}a sign for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter{/idea}. It points to a Day when all people, the first and last, are gathered. Ibn Kathir says angels and messengers will be present, and {reward}the Most Just will not wrong anyone by an atom's weight{/reward}.
now: You stand in a packed stadium, or the crowd at Eid prayer, and feel small among thousands. {idea}Imagine every human ever, in one place.{/idea} Everyone seen. That thought can make your private choices feel very public.
old: What I do in private stays private.
new: There is a Day when everyone is gathered and everything is seen, so I live with that in view.
try: In the next crowd you are part of, remember the Day of gathering and make a quiet dua for it.

title: The Day is delayed only to a counted term.
subtitle: Not a minute more, not a minute less
then: The Day just described is not cancelled by being far away. {idea}Allah only delays it to a counted term{/idea}, a fixed time, as Ibn Kathir says, that {trap}cannot be increased or decreased{/trap}.
now: The deadline is months away, so you do not start. Then it is next week. {idea}A counted term is already counting.{/idea} Your own days are numbered the same way; every one used is one fewer.
old: There is plenty of time before I need to get serious.
new: My days and the Day are both counted, so I use the time I have now.
try: Do today one good thing you keep putting off for "later."

title: No one speaks except by His leave.
subtitle: A silent Day that splits into two
then: On that Day {idea}no soul will speak except by Allah's permission{/idea}. In the hadith of intercession, the Prophet ﷺ said even the messengers will only say: O Allah, save us, save us. People will be {trap}wretched{/trap} or {reward}happy{/reward}. Umar asked if it depended on deeds; the Prophet ﷺ said each person is eased toward what he was created for.
now: You are used to explaining yourself: to HR, to your parents, in the comments. You can usually talk your way through. {idea}On that Day, words are by permission only.{/idea} What speaks for you is what you did today.
old: I can always explain myself later.
new: On that Day my deeds speak, not my excuses, so I let them speak well now.
try: Do one good deed today quietly, without telling anyone, and let it speak for you later.

title: The wretched will be in the Fire, gasping.
subtitle: A sober glimpse of the losing side
then: Allah describes the wretched in the Fire. Ibn Abbas explained the two words as {trap}hard sounds of breathing out and breathing in{/trap}, from the distress they feel. Ibn Kathir adds: {idea}we seek refuge with Allah from such evil{/idea}.
now: You take an easy breath right now without thinking. In a hard workout, or a panic attack, you learn what it is to struggle for air. {idea}Every easy breath is a gift and a chance.{/idea} Use it to turn toward Him.
old: Thinking about the Fire is too heavy; better to avoid it.
new: Allah describes it so I seek refuge and change course while I still can.
try: After your next prayer, say: O Allah, protect me from the Fire, three times.

title: As long as the heavens and earth endure.
subtitle: Lasting, except what your Lord wills
then: Ibn Jarir said the Arabs used "as long as the heavens and earth endure" to mean forever. Then comes {reward}except what your Lord wills{/reward}. Many scholars said this refers to sinful believers in tawhid, brought out by intercession, and even those whose only good was {reward}saying La ilaha illallah{/reward}.
now: You feel your sins are too many to ever be forgiven. Your record feels like a debt you cannot pay. {reward}The one word of tawhid carries enormous weight.{/reward} Hold on to it, and build on it.
old: If I have sinned badly, there is no hope left for me.
new: Allah does what He wills, and His mercy reaches even those with very little good, if they held to tawhid.
try: Say La ilaha illallah slowly and sincerely ten times today, thinking about its meaning.

title: A gift that is never cut off.
subtitle: The happy ones in Paradise, forever
then: The blessed, the followers of the messengers, will be in Paradise forever. Ibn Kathir says Allah ended with {reward}a gift without an end{/reward} so no one would think it could stop. The Prophet ﷺ said the people of Paradise will be told they will {reward}live and never die, stay young, healthy and never grieve{/reward}.
now: The holiday ends, the new phone gets old, the best day is followed by Monday. Every joy here has an expiry date. {reward}Imagine one that never does.{/reward} That is what your small good deeds are aimed at.
new: The joy Allah promises the believers is a gift that never ends.
try: When a good moment ends today, say: O Allah, give me the joy that never ends.

title: They worship only what their fathers worshipped.
subtitle: Copying without knowing is no foundation
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ not to doubt that the polytheists' worship is false. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they had no support for it except copying their fathers in ignorance{/trap}. Allah will give everyone their portion in full.
now: You do some things because "our family always does it": the way you spend at weddings, the grudges, even parts of worship you never asked about. {idea}Inherited is not the same as checked.{/idea} Keep what is true, question what is only habit.
old: If my family has always done it, it must be right.
new: I need to know why I do what I do, not just that my elders did it.
try: Pick one family custom and look up whether it truly has a basis in the deen.

title: Musa's Book was disputed too.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ facing denial
then: Allah reminds the Prophet ﷺ that {idea}He gave Musa the Book, and people differed over it{/idea}. So he has an example in earlier prophets and should not grieve. Ibn Jarir said that {trap}if the judgment had not been delayed to a set time{/trap}, it would have been decided immediately.
now: You share something true and beneficial and get mocked, or ignored, by your own family. You wonder if you said it wrong. {idea}Even revealed Books were argued over.{/idea} Rejection does not make the truth less true.
old: If people argue against the truth I share, I must have failed.
new: Disagreement over truth is an old pattern; my job is to stay patient and sincere.
try: When someone rejects a good word from you today, let it go without bitterness.

title: Every one of them is paid in full.
subtitle: Nothing small or great is overlooked

row.title: everything
sub: small and great, fine and ugly

then: Allah will gather the early and later generations and {idea}repay each of them their deeds in full{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says He knows all of them: {reward}their honorable deeds{/reward} and {trap}their despicable deeds{/trap}, the small and the great.
now: The extra minute you stayed to help a coworker. The snide remark in the family group. The coin you gave without anyone seeing. {idea}None of it is lost.{/idea} That is a warning and a huge comfort at once.
old: Small acts, good or bad, do not really count.
new: Allah knows every small deed and repays it fully, so nothing good I do is wasted.
try: Do one tiny good deed today that no one will notice, trusting that He does.
